en: Judged by comparing one thing with another; or the form of an adjective showing more of a quality.
ex: The study offers a comparative analysis of the two systems.
這項研究對兩個系統做了比較分析。

en: A person who is taking an exam.
ex: Each examinee must show an ID card at the door.
每位考生都必須在門口出示身分證。

en: Playful in a way that causes trouble but not serious harm; or intending to cause harm.
ex: The mischievous boy hid his sister's shoes.
那個調皮的男孩把姊姊的鞋子藏了起來。

en: To read something quickly to get the main ideas; or to move lightly over a surface.
ex: I skimmed the report before the meeting.
我在會議前快速瀏覽了報告。

en: Needing or depending on something or someone.
ex: The region is heavily reliant on tourism.
該地區嚴重依賴觀光業。

en: To die, especially in a sudden or violent way; or (of materials) to decay and be destroyed.
ex: Many climbers perished on the mountain in the storm.
許多登山客在暴風雨中喪生於山上。

en: To spoil the beauty or quality of something.
ex: A few mistakes marred an otherwise perfect performance.
幾個失誤破壞了原本完美的表演。

en: A feeling of excitement or worry while waiting to find out what will happen.
ex: The film kept the audience in suspense until the end.
這部電影讓觀眾直到結尾都懸著一顆心。

en: A small cupboard with a lock, used for keeping personal things at a school, gym or station.
ex: He kept his books in his locker at school.
他把書放在學校的置物櫃裡。

en: A human being who will die someday; or causing death.
ex: All mortals must die someday.
所有凡人終有一死。

en: An instrument that measures temperature.
ph: take a temperature with a thermometer
ex: The nurse put a thermometer under his tongue.
護理師把溫度計放到他舌頭下面。

en: To form an opinion or reach a conclusion from evidence rather than direct statement.
ex: From his tone, I inferred that he was angry.
從他的語氣，我推斷他很生氣。

en: A water plant with large, round leaves and beautiful flowers, important in Asian cultures.
ex: Lotus flowers bloomed across the pond in summer.
夏天，蓮花在整座池塘盛開。

en: A complete list of things in a place, or the goods a shop has in stock.
ex: The store closes for a day every year to take inventory.
這家店每年會休業一天來盤點存貨。

en: A small, smooth, round stone, often found on a beach or in a river.
ex: The child threw a pebble into the pond.
孩子往池塘裡扔了一顆小石子。

en: A person who had a job or position before someone else; or something that came before another.
col: follow in the footsteps of one's predecessor
ex: The new director is more popular than her predecessor.
新任主任比她的前任更受歡迎。

en: A problem that delays or stops progress.
ex: The delay was a major setback for the project.
這次延誤對專案造成重大挫折。

en: To kill an important person, especially for political reasons.
ex: President Kennedy was assassinated in 1963.
甘迺迪總統於1963年遭到暗殺。

en: Unfair treatment or a situation in which people are treated unfairly.
ex: They marched to protest racial injustice.
他們遊行抗議種族不公。

en: A junior officer in the army or navy; or a person who acts for someone else in authority.
ex: The lieutenant ordered his men to hold their position.
中尉命令他的部下堅守陣地。

en: Hair that grows on a man's upper lip.
ex: He grew a mustache to look older.
他蓄鬍子好讓自己看起來成熟些。

en: An official who follows rules strictly and is thought to be slow and unhelpful.
ex: Bureaucrats took months to approve the request.
官僚們花了幾個月才批准這項申請。

en: Made to be thrown away after use; or available for use or spending.
ex: We use disposable cups at the picnic to save washing up.
我們在野餐時用免洗杯以省去洗碗。

en: To produce a crop or profit; or to stop resisting and give in to pressure.
ex: The investment yielded a ten percent return.
這項投資帶來百分之十的收益。

en: A dish of meat or vegetables cooked in a spicy sauce, often served with rice, popular in South Asia.
ex: We ordered a spicy chicken curry with rice.
我們點了一份辣咖哩雞配米飯。

en: To make yourself or someone else get used to a new situation.
ex: It took him a while to accustom himself to the cold weather.
他花了一段時間才適應寒冷的天氣。

en: A short text beside a picture or photograph that explains it; or the words shown at the bottom of a screen.
ex: The caption under the picture named everyone in the photo.
照片下方的說明寫出了照片中每個人的名字。

en: To shine with small, quick flashes of light.
ex: Stars twinkled in the clear night sky.
晴朗的夜空中星星閃爍。

en: To take something out, often with effort; or a short piece taken from a longer book or text.
ex: The dentist extracted two of his teeth.
牙醫拔了他兩顆牙。

en: To want something very much, especially something you cannot easily have.
ex: She yearned for the quiet life of the countryside.
她渴望鄉村的寧靜生活。

en: Very generous or luxurious; or to give a lot of something to someone.
ex: They threw a lavish wedding party for two hundred guests.
他們為兩百位賓客舉辦了一場豪華的婚宴。

en: To make someone feel annoyed or angry; or to make part of the body sore.
ex: The smoke irritated my eyes and made them water.
煙刺激我的眼睛使它流淚。

en: A tree or plant that has green leaves all year round; or lasting and always popular.
ex: Pine and fir are common evergreen trees.
松樹和冷杉是常見的常綠樹。

en: The fold of skin that covers and protects your eye when it is closed.
ex: His eyelids grew heavy and he fell asleep.
他的眼皮越來越沉，然後睡著了。

en: A person or group that goes with someone to protect or guide them; or to go with someone to a place.
ex: Police escorted the prisoner to the courthouse.
警察把犯人押送到法院。

en: Extreme and often uncontrolled anger.
ex: He slammed the door in a fury.
他怒不可遏地摔上了門。

en: A lack of interest, care or concern about something.
ex: His indifference to other people's feelings upset her.
他對別人感受的漠不關心令她難過。

en: A place where roads, railway lines or pipes meet; or a point where things are joined.
ex: Turn left at the next junction.
在下個路口左轉。

en: The act of closing a business or road; or the feeling that a difficult experience has finished.
ex: The closure of the factory left hundreds without jobs.
工廠關閉使數百人失業。

en: Not necessary; able to be done without.
ex: In a budget crisis, many services become dispensable.
在預算危機時，許多服務變成可有可無。
